slice: toolchain (tools/ 16 py, .githooks/, apps/, configs/, catalogue/, funnels/, templates/)
summary: This slice is the operator/measurement toolchain plus the repo's shipped scaffolding, and it is in better shape than its reputation: 12 of 16 tools/ modules have a real consumer (tests, daedalus/health.py, daedalus/status.py, daedalus/spine/bootstrap.py, or another tool), the git hooks are actually installed (core.hooksPath=.githooks) and route through tools/iron_plan_guard.py, and apps/web is served by daedalus/web_api.py and exercised by tools/gui_check.py. The one systemic defect is a Gate-0 invariant-1/8 gap that the repo's own checker reports as a BLOCKER: 12 tools/ entrypoints are effectful and are NOT in daedalus/spine/effect_boundary.py's canonical registry, so the measurement harness that produces promotion receipts sits outside the effect boundary it measures. The second real defect is templates/agentenv.json, which ships a policy block with no write_allow key -- and daedalus/sensitivity.py:761 states that an empty write_allow means UNCONFINED, so any repo bootstrapped from the shipped template is write-unconfined while its comment claims fail-closed. Genuine islands are few: tools/guarded_call.py (zero callers anywhere), tools/lane_invariants.py and tools/audit_swarm.py (one-shot 2026-07-30 forensics, referenced only from archived docs and funnel specs), and catalogue/gui (only daedalus/gui_catalogue.py and its test read it; no CLI or web surface exposes it).

issues: NO `write_allow` KEY. daedalus/sensitivity.py:12-13 says the write axis is 'NOT fail-closed by default': an empty write_allow means unconfined, and sensitivity.py:761 states 'Empty write_allow therefore means unconfined'; sensitivity.py:774 only applies the fence `if policy.write_allow`. So a repo bootstrapped from this template is WRITE-UNCONFINED while its own `_comment` (line 2) claims 'With no policy block, the bench is read/advise-only (fail-closed)' and its `allow` list (lines 11-17) reads like a write restriction.

This repo's own .agentenv/agentenv.json documents the measurement that made write_allow necessary ('with allow-only, 8 of 12 paths this policy claims to deny were writable, including daedalus/config.py'). That lesson never reached the shipped template.
Template also lacks default_deny, high_risk_paths content, and test_timeout_s -- the live policy documents test_timeout_s as the fix for a configuration that was STRUCTURALLY unable to pass.

integration_gaps: GATE-0 BLOCKER, measured on this revision: `python tools/effect_boundary_check.py` reports 12 entrypoint.unregistered BLOCKERs -- tools.{audit_swarm,bootstrap_receipt,funnel,funnel_report,gate_discrimination,gate_host_preflight,gui_check,iron_plan_guard,iron_plan_hook_runner,lane_invariants,mutation_score,operability_drill}:main are effectful entrypoints outside daedalus/spine/effect_boundary.py's canonical registry. daedalus/spine/effect_boundary.py:916-931 added 'tools' to SCAN_PACKAGES precisely to make this visible; the discovery landed, the registration never did. Invariant 1 (one kernel) and Invariant 8 (bounded effects at the effect boundary) are both open here.

templates/agentenv.json ships a policy with no write_allow, and daedalus/sensitivity.py:761,774 make an absent write_allow mean UNCONFINED. Every repo onboarded from the shipped template gets an unconfined write axis behind a comment claiming fail-closed. The lesson is documented in this repo's own .agentenv/agentenv.json and never propagated to the template.

tools/guarded_call.py has zero callers: the process-boundary egress door was built for a DSPy/GEPA optimiser environment that does not exist in this tree. A guard nobody calls is the exact 'built but inert' failure tools/operability_drill.py's docstring was written about.

tools/lane_invariants.py (7 deterministic assertions over recorded lane runs) has zero code or test references. The 2026-07-30 failures it encodes -- byte-identical votes, template answers, refusals counted as answers -- would be invisible again today.

catalogue/gui/ is read only by daedalus/gui_catalogue.py and its unit test. No CLI subcommand, web endpoint, or agent path exposes the catalogue, so the 'available parts as data' idea is implemented and unreachable.

tools/gui_check.py is invoked only by path from tools/system_check.py:724 and has no test of its own; nothing verifies that the browser acceptance layer itself can still go red -- the same 'a check that never went red is a claim' rule that tools/self_test.py exists to enforce for system_check.

tools/self_test.py:40 uses a bare `import system_check as sc` with no sys.path setup, so `python -m tools.self_test` raises ModuleNotFoundError; the mutation control is reachable only via tools/system_check.py or a direct script invocation from tools/.

apps/web/dist/ is committed with no .gitignore entry and no build-freshness check. daedalus/web_api.py:984 serves a placeholder when dist is absent, and tools/gui_check.py names that placeholder as the case naive checks pass on -- a stale committed bundle is checked as if it were the product.
notable: The slice's non-BLOCKER health is good: 12 of 16 tools/ modules have a verified consumer in daedalus/ or tests/, and .githooks is genuinely installed (core.hooksPath=.githooks), so the plan guard runs on every ordinary commit.

Three 'seed a defect in a disposable clone' implementations coexist: tools/self_test.py, tools/mutation_score.py, and tools/gate_discrimination.py (plus runs/ab/oracle_check.py). Each docstring argues it generalised the previous two rather than adding a third shape, and gate_discrimination.py:931 does reuse system_check.Sandbox -- but this is the slice's largest consolidation opportunity (~2300 lines across the three).

The docstrings in this slice are unusually high-value evidence: tools/bootstrap_receipt.py:1-30 records the Windows spawn incident (10 parallel attempts, intent_ids 56-64), tools/funnel_report.py:1-20 records the 715-answers/692-identical measurement, tools/lane_invariants.py:1-27 records 8 model refuters producing 0 findings vs 2 AST functions catching 3/3. These are retained negative evidence per AGENTS.md rule 5 and should survive any cleanup.

Stale module docstring: daedalus/spine/effect_boundary.py:921 states '18 of 19 python files under tools/ is an entrypoint'. tools/ now holds 16 python files, and the current run flags 12. The narrative is right, the arithmetic is dated.

tools/effect_boundary_check.py also surfaces a second live BLOCKER outside my slice: entrypoint.effect_drift on daedalus.providers.ollama:OllamaProvider.rollback -- new undeclared effects network_egress, process_spawn. Routing to the providers slice.

tools/audit_swarm.py encodes an owner-lifted egress allow-list from 2026-07-30 as the file's standing configuration rather than as a one-run parameter; re-running it inherits the lift by default. Its structural protection (file list from `git ls-files daedalus`, never a filesystem walk, so gitignored .captures/ with Edge Login Data cannot enter scope) is the right pattern and should be stated as a rule somewhere less perishable than one script's docstring.
funnels/today/ and funnels/claims123/ are dated one-day scopes checked into the repo as configuration; every path they name still resolves, but they are run history in a config directory.
configs/ contains exactly one example file and catalogue/ exactly one subdirectory -- both are directories created for a single artifact each.
